project.name: lpc-toolkit
project.description: An LPC character spritesheet toolkit that loads a catalog of layered art, lets users configure a character, composes and recolors sprites through an environment-agnostic core, and exports rendered assets with mandatory attribution metadata.

nodes.name: Asset Catalog Management
nodes.summary: This domain turns migrated LPC definitions, palettes, spritesheets, and release metadata into the runtime catalog used by the character editor. It also verifies and packages asset snapshots so browser consumers receive consistent, traceable inputs.

businessRules: Only validated asset definitions and spritesheets should enter the runtime catalog.
Catalog aliases and segmented targets must resolve to composable items.
Released asset files must match their manifest and expected hashes.
crossDomainInteractions: Supplies selectable items and palettes to Character Configuration.
Supplies image paths and metadata to Sprite Composition.
Supplies credit-bearing asset metadata to Attribution and Licensing.

nodes.name: Character Configuration
nodes.summary: This domain manages the user's layered character choices, including initial selections, direct picks, presets, random outfits, animation choices, and shareable URL state. It converts editor state into the core selection model consumed by composition.

businessRules: Selections must remain compatible with the chosen body type, animation, and catalog item capabilities.
Selection order determines the visual layer stack.
Serialized URL state must restore supported selections without corrupting current editor state.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes catalog items and palettes from Asset Catalog Management.
Provides ordered selections to Sprite Composition.
Provides export scope and selected items to Export and Delivery.

nodes.name: Sprite Composition
nodes.summary: This domain resolves selected LPC layers, applies palette recoloring and frame rules, and draws composed character output. Its core contracts receive image-loading and canvas capabilities from callers, preserving an environment-agnostic composition engine.

businessRules: The core must not depend directly on browser, DOM, filesystem, or Node canvas APIs.
Layer order, animation geometry, and recolor mappings determine the rendered pixels.
Every successful composition must carry credit metadata for the assets that contributed pixels.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes asset definitions and images from Asset Catalog Management.
Consumes ordered selections from Character Configuration.
Requests mandatory credit metadata from Attribution and Licensing.
Provides rendered canvases and frames to Export and Delivery.

nodes.name: Attribution and Licensing
nodes.summary: This domain identifies the source credits and effective license obligations associated with the assets used in a composition. It formats attribution for human-readable and machine-readable delivery so rendered sprites remain accompanied by required credit metadata.

businessRules: Every rendered sprite must be accompanied by credit metadata derived from the asset credits catalog.
Credits must be matched to the actual sprite paths used by the composition.
The effective license must reflect the obligations of all contributing assets.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes used asset paths and item metadata from Sprite Composition.
Consumes source credit metadata from Asset Catalog Management.
Supplies attribution files and license summaries to Export and Delivery.

nodes.name: Export and Delivery
nodes.summary: This domain converts composed LPC output into downloadable PNG and ZIP deliverables organized by animation, item, or frame. It packages the corresponding attribution metadata with exported sprites and triggers browser downloads.

businessRules: Exported pixel assets must include the attribution metadata associated with their composition.
File names and archive structure must identify the exported animation, item, or frame.
Browser-specific encoding and download behavior must remain outside the environment-agnostic core.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes configured selections from Character Configuration.
Consumes rendered canvases and frame data from Sprite Composition.
Consumes credit and license documents from Attribution and Licensing.

nodes.name: Load Runtime Catalog
nodes.summary: Build the browser's searchable catalog and palette metadata from packaged LPC definition records.

nodes.name: Normalize Definition Keys
nodes.summary: Normalize packaged definition paths before converting them into catalog records.

nodes.name: Create Catalog
nodes.summary: Resolve catalog item aliases and segmented targets into the runtime catalog of composable items.

nodes.name: Load Catalog Records
nodes.summary: Adapt packaged definition records into the browser runtime catalog and surface catalog warnings.

nodes.name: Load Palette Records
nodes.summary: Build runtime palette metadata from packaged palette records for recolorable character layers.

nodes.name: Prepare Asset Snapshot
nodes.summary: Acquire, verify, and materialize a release snapshot of LPC assets for browser packaging.

nodes.name: Load Release Configuration
nodes.summary: Read the asset release configuration that identifies the snapshot and expected manifest.

nodes.name: Download Release
nodes.summary: Retrieve the configured asset archive for local verification and materialization.

nodes.name: Verify Manifest and Hashes
nodes.summary: Verify archive entries and file hashes against the release manifest before accepting asset data.

nodes.name: Materialize Assets
nodes.summary: Write the verified snapshot into the asset layout consumed by the web package.

nodes.name: Initialize Character
nodes.summary: Create the initial character selection and restore compatible shared state from the browser URL.

nodes.name: Read URL State
nodes.summary: Read the current browser hash as the source of potentially shared character configuration.

nodes.name: Parse Shared Selection
nodes.summary: Parse the initial URL hash into supported character state and selection values.

nodes.name: Choose Required Layers
nodes.summary: Build required initial selections for the character when shared state is absent or incomplete.

nodes.name: Synchronize URL
nodes.summary: Keep reducer selections and browser navigation synchronized through serialized hash state.

nodes.name: Customize Character Layers
nodes.summary: Apply direct item choices, presets, or randomized outfits to the ordered character layer selection.

nodes.name: Filter Compatible Items
nodes.summary: Limit available catalog choices to items compatible with the current body type and animation constraints.

nodes.name: Build Selection Action
nodes.summary: Translate an item choice into a reducer action that picks or clears the corresponding layer.

nodes.name: Apply Preset or Random Outfit
nodes.summary: Replace clothing choices from a preset or construct a randomized compatible outfit.

nodes.name: Update Selection State
nodes.summary: Apply layer, animation, direction, playback, and reset actions to editor selection state.

nodes.name: Order Selected Layers
nodes.summary: Return non-empty selections in the order used by the layer stack and composition pipeline.

nodes.name: Compose Character
nodes.summary: Resolve selected asset layers, recolor their pixels, draw them through caller-supplied adapters, and return structured composition output with credits.

nodes.name: Convert Editor Selections
nodes.summary: Convert UI selection entries into the environment-agnostic core selection model.

nodes.name: Resolve Selected Layers
nodes.summary: Resolve selected catalog items into ordered sprite layers and paths for the requested character state.

nodes.name: Resolve Recolor Palettes
nodes.summary: Normalize recolor choices and resolve base and target palette mappings for selected layers.

nodes.name: Draw Composed Output
nodes.summary: Load images and draw recolored layers through injected image and canvas adapter capabilities.

nodes.name: Attach Credit Metadata
nodes.summary: Collect the credit records for the sprite paths used in the completed composition.

nodes.name: Render Animation Output
nodes.summary: Choose a supported animation and transform composed spritesheet data into animation frames or a full-sheet preview.

nodes.name: Choose Supported Animation
nodes.summary: Choose a valid standard, custom, or fallback animation for the current composition.

nodes.name: Extract Animation
nodes.summary: Extract the requested animation from composed spritesheet output.

nodes.name: Slice Animation Frames
nodes.summary: Slice standard or custom spritesheet regions into individual frame canvases.

nodes.name: Render Full Sheet
nodes.summary: Draw a full composed spritesheet with transparency treatment for preview or export.

nodes.name: Derive Composition Attribution
nodes.summary: Map the sprite paths used by a composition to credit records and determine the resulting license obligations.

nodes.name: Collect Used Sprite Paths
nodes.summary: Derive the concrete sprite paths represented by the current ordered selections.

nodes.name: Match Credit Records
nodes.summary: Match each used sprite path to its applicable source credit metadata.

nodes.name: Aggregate Credits
nodes.summary: Aggregate and return the contributor and source records required for the composition.

nodes.name: Compute Effective License
nodes.summary: Determine the effective license obligations across all contributing asset credit records.

nodes.name: Format Attribution Files
nodes.summary: Convert composition credit metadata into text and CSV representations suitable for delivery with sprites.

nodes.name: Receive Composition Credits
nodes.summary: Use the credit metadata attached to the composed sprite result as the attribution source.

nodes.name: Format Text Credits
nodes.summary: Format contributor, source, and license metadata as a human-readable text attribution document.

nodes.name: Format CSV Credits
nodes.summary: Format credit metadata as CSV for machine-readable inclusion in exported deliverables.

nodes.name: Export Animation Archive
nodes.summary: Encode composed animation output as PNG files, add attribution metadata, and assemble a downloadable ZIP archive.

nodes.name: Extract Export Frames
nodes.summary: Extract the selected animation frames from composed character output.

nodes.name: Encode PNG Files
nodes.summary: Encode the frame canvases as PNG blobs for inclusion in the export archive.

nodes.name: Add Attribution
nodes.summary: Include the composition's required credit and license metadata alongside exported animation files.

nodes.name: Build Animation ZIP
nodes.summary: Organize encoded frames and metadata into an animation-named ZIP archive.

nodes.name: Download Archive
nodes.summary: Trigger the browser download for the completed animation archive.

nodes.name: Export Layered Assets
nodes.summary: Export configured character assets grouped by contributing item or by individual frame while preserving layer metadata and attribution.

domainMeta.entryPoint: Export by item or frame action

nodes.name: Resolve Selected Item Metadata
nodes.summary: Look up metadata for the items represented by the current character selections.

nodes.name: Build Single-Item Selections
nodes.summary: Create per-item selection sets used to render isolated contributing layers.

nodes.name: Render Item Assets
nodes.summary: Render and encode composition output grouped by each selected contributing item.

nodes.name: Render Frame Assets
nodes.summary: Render and encode composition output grouped by individual spritesheet frame.

nodes.name: Package Metadata and Credits
nodes.summary: Package item layer metadata and required attribution with the rendered asset files.

nodes.name: Download Layered Archive
nodes.summary: Trigger the browser download for the completed item- or frame-organized archive.

edges.description: The runtime catalog and palettes define the items and color choices available to the character editor.
Validated definitions and spritesheets provide the source layers resolved and drawn by composition.
Asset metadata supplies the credit records matched to sprites used in a composition.
Ordered character selections, animation, direction, and recolor choices form the composition request.
Composition reports the concrete asset paths used so mandatory credits and effective licensing can be derived.
Composed sheets, animations, frames, and isolated layers become the pixel content of exports.
Formatted credit and license metadata accompanies every exported sprite deliverable.
The active selection determines which animations, items, and frames are included in an export.
